item.title: Thailand’s Inflation Accelerates Past Central Bank’s Target
item.content:encoded: Thailand’s consumer inflation accelerated more than expected in October, exceeding the central bank’s target range as higher fuel prices driven by the Middle East conflict pushed up living costs.

item.title: Malaysia’s Central Bank Holds Rate Steady, Cites Resilient Growth
item.content:encoded: The central bank expects Malaysia’s economy to grow more than 5% in 2026 and remain resilient in 2027.

item.title: Eurozone Inflation Rises to 4%, Driven by Energy Costs
item.content:encoded: Inflation in the eurozone reached double the European Central Bank’s target in October as energy costs continued to rise.

item.title: U.S. Home-Builder Sentiment Sinks to 14-Year Low
item.content:encoded: The NAHB/Wells Fargo Housing Market Index, a gauge of builder confidence in the market for newly built single family housing, fell three points to 29 in October. That’s the lowest reading since June 2012.

item.title: America’s home-buying market is a house divided as surging mortgage rates send many buyers to the sidelines, while the affluent drive overall prices higher with big cash purchases
item.content:encoded: Surging mortgage rates are sending many buyers to the sidelines, while affluent shoppers are driving overall prices higher with big cash purchases.

item.title: U.S. Factory Activity Expands in October
item.content:encoded: The Institute for Supply Management’s purchasing managers’ index was 55.5 in October – higher than the September figure of 54.5.

item.title: Canada Retail Sales Look to Build on August’s Rebound
item.content:encoded: Retail spending by Canadians looks to have remained on the rise last month, though the pace is showing signs of cooling as uncertainty and gasoline prices remain high.

item.title: Consumer Sentiment Declined Slightly in October
item.content:encoded: The University of Michigan survey’s headline index came in at 48, down from 48.1 in September and hovering near record-low levels.

item.title: U.K. Consumer Confidence Suffers Biggest Drop Since Pandemic
item.content:encoded: Consumer sentiment tumbled at the fastest pace since the Covid-19 pandemic this month as mounting cost-of-living pressures reversed the bounce in optimism seen over the summer.

item.title: Eurozone Swung to Goods-Trade Deficit in August
item.content:encoded: Trade in the eurozone swung to a deficit in August as higher energy imports and weaker machinery and vehicle trade weighed on the balance.

item.title: There is a whiff of postelection optimism about the housing market that is boosting the battered shares of home builders in an otherwise volatile stock market
item.content:encoded: D.R. Horton, PulteGroup and Lennar have all outperformed since Tuesday’s midterm elections.

item.title: New Zealand’s Jobless Rate Climbs Ahead Of Election
item.content:encoded: The unemployment rate rose to 5.7%, its highest level since mid-2015, defying expectations of a fall and affirming the central bank’s recent caution around raising interest rates further.

item.title: Swiss Inflation Jumps to Highest Since 2023 as Energy Costs Climb
item.content:encoded: Annual inflation was 1.5% in October, compared with 1.0% in the prior month, Switzerland’s statistics office said.

item.title: The U.S. is in a battle to lower the costs to build housing, but it’s losing—as factors including the Iran war and tariffs fuel rising expenses for home builders
item.content:encoded: The Iran war, tariffs and the AI build-out have pushed up the costs of materials, labor and borrowing.

item.title: U.S. Housing Starts Dropped Again in September
item.content:encoded: Housing starts fell 5.2% in September to 1.221 million. Economists had expected a reading of 1.3 million and for starts to rise 2% over the month.

item.title: Brazil’s Central Bank Stops Easing Cycle as Inflation Remains High
item.content:encoded: Brazil’s central bank held its steep interest rates unchanged after five consecutive cuts as inflation drifted away from target amid growing concern around government spending.

item.title: Australia Central Bank Raises Interest Rates to Highest Level in 18 Years
item.content:encoded: The Reserve Bank of Australia raised interest rates by 25 basis points to 4.85%, the highest since 2008 after “materially” revising up its inflation forecasts.

item.title: German Consumers Grow Slightly Gloomier on Lingering Inflation Concerns
item.content:encoded: The country’s consumer-climate index fell to minus 30.8 in its forecast for November, from minus 30.6 in October.

item.title: U.S. Trade Deficit Contracted in September
item.content:encoded: Imports were higher than exports by $105 billion, down 0.7% from August, in contrast to economists’ expectations for the trade gap to widen.

item.title: Capital Account: President Trump once called “tariff” the most beautiful word in the dictionary. He has somehow made it one of the most hated words in politics, writes @greg_ip
item.content:encoded: President Trump’s tariffs collided with public anxiety over the cost of living. Now his trade legacy is at risk.
